newsitem.title: FRANCE: Port grain silos hit by French truckers strike.
newsitem.headline: Port grain silos hit by French truckers strike.

text.p: A nationwide trucking strike is now starting to disrupt grain supplies to French ports, local silos officials said on Tuesday.
Truckers, who have been blockading roads, ports and fuel depots for the last nine days, are demanding a 10 percent wage rise, payment for all hours worked and the right to retire at 55.
In Rouen a local official at the UCASPOR silo said the situation worsened on Monday after truckers tightened their blockade on the A13 access highway.
"We are beginning to feel it today as most access roads are blocked but the main concern is petrol shortages," one official said.
Port officials said that while a few trucks were still bypassing road blockades, petrol shortages were now threatening to seriously curb port activity.
"The hunt for petrol is on ," one official said, explaining that soon port and silos employees may be unable to get to work.
In the northern port of Dunkirk local silos officials said trucks could still use the Paris-Lille highway and supply silos.
"We are mostly concerned over gasoline shortages as refineries are now sealed off," one official said.
He said silos were operating with tight stocks and that if the strike lasted one more week, ship loadings may be disrupted.
In the southwestern port of Bordeaux officials at the SIGMA silo said the strike was curtailing grain supplies activity.
But because silos are full of newly harvested maize, ship loadings would proceed as normal.
The nationwide traffic information centre counted 171 blockades on roads across the country.

In Normandy all petrol depots and refineries near Rouen were sealed off. In certain regions including the Pas-de-Calais, local officials have since Monday imposed rationing of petrol supplies to private car owners to avert possible shortages.
